envelope.text: Takes [`Severity`], not rclrs's `LogSeverity`: it has a `Trace` level rclrs

why:
LANDED phase-467 — `nros_log::Logger::set_default_level(Severity)`, an associated function exactly like rclrs's, moving ONE process-wide `AtomicU8` that every logger with no level of its own filters on. It was a `gap` until then, and the row was right about why the obvious fix was not one: `DEFAULT_LOGGER.set_level(..)` compiles and moves the threshold of the ONE logger named `"nros"`, not the level anything else starts at — the `PollingSubscription::take()` hazard in miniature, and RFC-0089 forbids closing a row that way.

It is retroactive, which is the part that needed a mechanism rather than a name: `Logger::new` now stores a SENTINEL meaning "no level of its own" instead of `Severity::Info`, so a `static LOGGER: Logger = Logger::new("x")` compiled into the image long before the call follows it, while `with_level(.., Info)` and `set_level(Info)` are not overridden. Before the sentinel those two were indistinguishable at registration, which is why applying a default there would have silently overridden an author's choice. Same mechanism as row `c:log_severity_t` (`UNSET` = inherit); the two were one change and landed together.

NOW A `divergence`, not a closed gap, and the bound is the PARAMETER TYPE. The report buckets it `arity-only`: ours takes `Severity`, rclrs's takes `LogSeverity`. The capability is identical — measured against rclrs's own source, `ros2_rust`'s `rclrs/src/logging/logger.rs` at **v0.7.0**, which is the version this lane compares against (`docs/reference/api-surface/rclrs.json` records its provenance as rclrs 0.7.0). There `set_default_level` is a one-line forward to `rcutils_logging_set_default_logger_level`, whose documented treatment of `UNSET` (restore `RCUTILS_DEFAULT_LOGGER_DEFAULT_LEVEL`, i.e. `INFO`) is what our C entry point `rclc_log_set_default_level` does. CITED BY PROJECT AND VERSION, not by the path a checkout happens to have it at: rclrs reaches this tree only as a layer-3 submodule of `play_launch`, which nano-ros initialises NON-recursively, so that path resolves in a checkout that once ran a recursive init and in no fresh clone. `check-ledger-orphan-refs` refused the path spelling for exactly that reason and was right to — the same shape as reading rcutils in the `ros2` box and citing it from the host. The types differ in both directions and each difference is already a row: ours adds `Trace`, which rclrs has no level for, and ours has NO `Unset` variant, which is `rust:Logger::unset_level`. `rust:Severity` records why there is nothing to correlate the type itself against — the recorded rclrs surface carries no `LogSeverity` RECORD, only references to it.

Held by `a_logger_with_no_level_of_its_own_follows_the_process_default` in `packages/core/nros-log/src/lib.rs`, which is deliberately ONE test: the default is process-wide state and this crate's tests are threads in one process, so a second test that moved it would race the first and the flake would read as a logic bug.

issue 1637 (2026-10-05) — ENVELOPE WRITTEN where a porting user reads it: the method's rustdoc now states the `Severity`-vs-`LogSeverity` parameter bound (extra `Trace`, no `Unset`, pass `Info` where rclrs passes `Unset`). `Severity`'s own rustdoc and `book/src/user-guide/logging.md` called it "mirroring"/"matching" `rcutils_log_severity_t`, which it does not (0..5 plus `Trace` and no `UNSET`, where rcutils is `UNSET=0, DEBUG=10 ... FATAL=50`); both are corrected.
